## Breaking changes

- `attach_project` and `detach_project` are gone. Attach mode is now `run_project({ attach: true })`, and `stop_project` ends both kinds of session.
- Every tool now returns one JSON object, as `structuredContent` and as the same JSON in a text block, and every tool declares an `outputSchema`. `take_screenshot` and `render_movie` also return image blocks next to it. Tools that used to answer with a sentence now answer with fields, and a handful of fields were renamed. See "Migration" below for the full list.
- Calls that used to report success for something that did not happen now return an error, or lead their payload with a `warnings` entry. The cases are listed under "Migration".
- A runtime tool never falls back to another project's session. If no session is current, or the current game has exited, it returns an error that lists the live sessions.
- `run_project` on a second project adds a session instead of stopping the first.
- Input that used to be ignored or half applied is now refused: an unknown `validate` key, a `batch_scene_operations` item with a missing or unknown `operation`, a fractional component on an integer vector, an out-of-range packed integer element, an invalid `search_project` `maxResults`, an `update_autoload` call that changes nothing, and an autoload path holding a quote or a line break. Under `GODOT_MCP_STRICT=true`, a launch whose scene cannot be found or resolved is refused too.
- Headless scene edits keep what the file held: an inherited scene stays inherited, an edit inside an instance writes only the property that changed, scene and `ext_resource` uids survive, and a script or exported value that names an autoload is no longer lost. `delete_nodes` refuses a node inherited from a base scene, and `add_node` now lets `properties` win over the top-level `position`, `rotation`, `scale`, `visible` and `modulate`.
- `batch_scene_operations` no longer rewrites every scene it names. The closing save writes a scene only if an operation on it succeeded and no `save` item has written it since. A `save` item with `newPath` onto a scene the batch has already changed and not yet written is refused as that item's error, because it would discard those changes.
- The server runs one runtime operation at a time. `run_project`, `switch_project`, the four runtime tools and the profiling tools go through one queue, so calls issued in parallel wait their turn, and a call that waits 30 seconds returns an error naming the operation it waited behind. `stop_project` does not queue: it ends the session at once, and the runtime call it cut off fails saying the session was stopped. The time a `run_project` waits for its turn comes out of its bridge wait, and a start left with under 10 seconds for the bridge is refused before anything is stopped or launched. `profile_project` holds the queue for its whole window: a `simulate_input` sent alongside it no longer runs during the capture. Use `start_profiler`, `simulate_input`, `stop_profiler` to drive the game while it is profiled.
- `profile_project` accepts a window of at most 30 seconds, down from 60, so the call answers inside a client's 60 second request timeout. `start_profiler` still takes up to 60.
- A number written to an integer must be finite, whole and within the range a JSON number carries exactly (up to 2^53). After an `int` property is assigned it is read back. A value outside 32 bits that the property did not keep is an error that leaves the property as it was. A value inside 32 bits that the property's setter changed or ignored (`z_index` above 4096) is a success led by a warning that names both numbers. Both used to be stored wrapped, saturated or truncated under a plain success.
- `list_autoloads` returns one entry per name, the assignment the engine keeps. It used to list a name once per line that assigned it. `remove_autoload` removes every assignment of the name and `update_autoload` edits the one the engine keeps.
- Path parameters are stricter in three places and looser in two. A file or folder name that ends in a dot or a space or is a Windows device name (`NUL`, `con.txt`, `COM1`), a colon outside the drive prefix, and a path to write that leaves the project through a symbolic link or junction are refused. A `..` that stays inside the project (`scenes/../main.tscn`) is now accepted, and so is a path that is only read or referenced (`texturePath`, `scriptPath`, an autoload path, a `scene` to run) when a link on the way leads out of the project, so a shared `addons/` folder linked in keeps working. Every path field of a `batch_scene_operations` item is checked the same way, where 3.8.1 checked only containment. Path errors share one wording: `Invalid <field>: "<path>" resolves outside the project or is not a valid file name`.
- The script scan blocks more. A reflective call with a literal method name is judged as the call it makes, so `OS.call("execute", ...)`, `OS.callv("execute", [...])` and `OS.call_deferred("execute", ...)` are Tier 1 like `OS.execute(...)`; they were Tier 3 warnings. `(OS).execute(...)`, `GDScript.new()`, `OS.create_instance`, `GDExtensionManager.load_extension` and a non-literal `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request` are Tier 1 as well. `set_script` on any receiver and a bare `call(name_var)` or `callv(name_var)` now ask for confirmation. So do `source_code`, `instance_from_id`, `JavaScriptBridge.eval`, and a guarded singleton or `GDScript` used as a value (`var o = OS`, `OS["execute"]`). A literal method name is decoded before it is judged (`OS.call("\u0065xecute")` is `OS.execute`), a dispatch that names another dispatch is followed (`OS.call("call", "execute")`), and `load(r"res://a.tscn")` is a literal like any other.
- `stop_project` with nothing to stop returns `Nothing to stop: no runtime session is current.` in place of `No active Godot process to stop.`
- A `simulate_input` batch whose time budget (its waits and holds, plus its frames at 10 fps) is over 600 seconds is refused before anything is injected. A wait in milliseconds used to have no limit.

## Migration

### Removed tools

| Before                                        | Now                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `attach_project({ projectPath, bridgePort })` | `run_project({ projectPath, attach: true, bridgePort })`. `scene` is rejected with `attach: true` whenever it is given, and `background` and `profiling` when they are `true`, instead of being ignored. `false` is accepted. The pre-flight script scan now runs in attach mode too, and under `GODOT_MCP_STRICT` a Tier 1 finding refuses to inject the bridge. The launch confirmation prompt does not apply, because nothing is launched. |
| `detach_project`                              | `stop_project`. It detaches an attached session without killing the Godot process and reports `externalProcessPreserved: true`. After an attached session has ended by itself (you closed the game), `detach_project` used to succeed; `stop_project` now returns its `Nothing to stop: no runtime session is current.` error, and nothing is left to clean up.                                                                               |

### Tools whose response form changed

| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `add_node`                                                             | Text: `Node 'X' of type 'T' added successfully`                                                                                                                                                                                     | `{ warnings?, nodeName, nodeType, nodePath }`, read back after the add. `warnings` leads when Godot renamed the node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `load_sprite`                                                          | Text sentence                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `{ nodePath, nodeType, texturePath }`, read back from the node                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `save_scene`                                                           | Text sentence                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `{ scenePath, savedScenePath }`, with the save confirmed on disk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `export_mesh_library`                                                  | Text sentence                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `{ warnings?, outputPath, itemCount, itemNames }`. `warnings` leads for requested names that were not exported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `connect_signal`, `disconnect_signal`                                  | Text sentence                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `{ warnings?, nodePath, signal, targetNodePath, method, connected }`. `connected` is read from the saved scene file. A connect the file does not hold, or a disconnect it still holds, is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `duplicate_node`                                                       | `{ success, originalPath, newPath }`                                                                                                                                                                                                | `{ success, nodePath, newNodePath }`. `newNodePath` is read back and always in `root/...` form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

The findings are the `warnings`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| `get_debug_output`                                                     | `attached: true` in attached mode only                                                                                                                                                                                              | `sessionMode` on every response, plus `projectPath`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The `runtime` block also gains `liveSessions[]`, `exitCode` (for a session whose process exited) and, when you pass a `projectPath`, `project`. `runtime.bridgeResponsive` can be `null`: another operation held the session queue, so the bridge was not pinged. |
| `get_scene_dependencies`                                               | `scene`, the path as the caller wrote it (`res://scenes/a.tscn`, or an absolute path)                                                                                                                                               | `scenePath`, the project-relative path (`scenes/a.tscn`), as in every other tool                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `get_scene_tree`                                                       | `path` built from the subtree root's own name (`Main/Label`)                                                                                                                                                                        | `path` in `root/...` form for every node, so a returned path resolves when passed back as a `nodePath`. A node `maxDepth` did not open has `children: null` and a `childCount` instead of `[]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `take_screenshot`                                                      | `{ responseMode, path, size, ... }`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Also `projectPath` and `stats` on every call, in all three response modes. `stats` is `null` with a leading warning when the PNG could not be measured. An image file over 3 MiB, or a full PNG that could not be decoded, is no longer returned inline: the path comes back with a leading warning. `previewMaxWidth` and `previewMaxHeight` above 1920 and 1080 are clamped.                                              |
| `get_project_files`                                                    | A directory cut by `maxDepth`, or unreadable, had `children: []`; links and junctions were dropped                                                                                                                                  | Such a directory has `children: null`; a link is `{ name, type: "link", path }` and is not followed. A `maxDepth` that is not an integer of -1 or more is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `search_project`                                                       | `{ matches, truncated }`, with `truncated: true` whenever the result reached `maxResults`                                                                                                                                           | Also `filesSearched` and `fileTypes`. `truncated` is `true` only when a further match existed beyond `maxResults`, so a search with exactly that many matches reports `false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `run_script`, `get_ui_elements`, `simulate_input`, the profiling tools |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `projectPath` names the session they acted on. `warnings` is now the first key of every payload that has one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `create_scene`, `attach_script`, `get_node_signals`                    | `scenePath`, `nodePath` and `scriptPath` repeated the argument as it was written                                                                                                                                                    | `scenePath` and `scriptPath` are project-relative and `nodePath` is in `root/...` form, whichever way they were passed. `attach_script({ nodePath: "Player", scriptPath: "res://p.gd" })` returns `nodePath: "root/Player"` and `scriptPath: "p.gd"`.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `stop_project`                                                         | Called on a game that had exited and whose logs an earlier `stop_project` had already returned, while a finished profiler capture was still held, it released the capture and returned an error saying there was no process to stop | A success: `message` says the capture was released, `alreadyExited` is `true`, and `finalOutput` and `finalErrors` are `null` with a leading warning that the earlier call returned them. With nothing retained it is still an error.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `run_script`                                                           | `{ projectPath, success, result, tip, warnings? }`, with `success: true` on every success                                                                                                                                           | `success` is gone: `{ projectPath, result, tip, warnings? }`. A failure is an error response, so the field carried nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

The shared names are `projectPath`, `scenePath`, `nodePath`, `sessionMode` and `warnings`. `docs/tools.md` has the full conventions.

### Behavior changes in sessions

- `run_project` on a second project adds a session and makes it current. Sessions on other projects keep running.
- The runtime tools (`take_screenshot`, `simulate_input`, `get_ui_elements`, `run_script`), the profiling tools, `get_debug_output` and `stop_project` act on the current session. `switch_project({ projectPath })` changes which one is current. `stop_project` stops the current session and leaves none current.
- When no session is current, or the current game has exited, these tools return an error that lists the live sessions and points at `switch_project`. Nothing is picked for you.
- Scene and node edits are refused while any session is live on the project, current or not, and the refusal says to `switch_project` first when it is not the current one.
- The error for a bridge that never answered now names the port it waited on instead of `null`.
- A `run_project` that fails before it launches anything leaves the session that was current still current, and the session it would have replaced still running. A game whose bridge never answers is torn down and leaves no session current. A game that exits during startup is not torn down: it stays current with its logs kept.
- A spawned `run_project` on a project where this server holds an attached session detaches that session first. The bridge in the Godot you launched is told to shut down, that Godot keeps running, and `message` says so. If its bridge does not acknowledge, `warnings` leads with that.
- For that game, the one that exits before its bridge is ready, `get_debug_output` reads the captured logs after the error and `run_project` can be retried without `stop_project`.
- When another host registered the session that blocks an edit, a render or a start, the refusal names that host and the owner file under `.mcp/godot-runtime/bridge/owners/` to delete if the session is known to be gone. A session registered from another host cannot be probed, so it counts as live.
- A spawned game is killed as a process tree on `stop_project` and when the server exits, so the Windows console wrapper and launcher scripts no longer leave the real game running with the bridge port held. Outside Windows the game and every headless run lead their own process group, so the kill reaches a wrapper script's engine too.
- A spawned game quits by itself within a few seconds of its server dying, including a server that was killed outright. An attached Godot is never told to quit.
- A bridge owner is judged by its pid and by the start identity it recorded for itself, which the operating system fixes when the process is created, so the owner file of a server that was killed, whose pid another process now holds, no longer blocks edits or strands the bridge. When the identity cannot be read the pid answer stands.
- On Linux and macOS a server whose terminal closes (`SIGHUP`) shuts down as it does on `SIGTERM`, stopping its games and headless runs instead of leaving them running.
- In an attached session, a failed command ends the session only when the follow-up probe itself fails as a disconnect. A probe that times out is a game that is alive and busy, and the session stands.

## New

- `render_movie` renders a short fixed number of frames in a separate Godot run under the engine's movie writer, with no bridge, no input and no session, and reports what rendered. It has three modes. `check` (the default) measures the frames and reports `likelyBlank`, `motion` and `anyMotion` with a few downscaled inline frames, then deletes the files. Blankness and motion are decided over every pixel, not on a sample grid. `likelyBlank` means the last frame is one flat color, within 8 of 255 per channel. A pair of frames shows motion when enough pixels changed by more than 8 of 255 on any channel: 4 for a frame up to 1152x648, and more in proportion for a larger one, so a small moving element is detected and noise on a large frame is not; each `motionPairs` entry carries `changedPixels`, `changedFraction`, the `motionThreshold` it was held to and `changedBounds`, the rectangle holding every changed pixel, and `motion` stays the largest mean difference, which can read near 0 while `anyMotion` is `true`. `bytesWritten` is the size of everything the run wrote. `frames` keeps the PNG frames under `.mcp/godot-runtime/movies/` and returns their paths. `video` keeps one `avi` or `ogv` file. It needs a display, goes through the same pre-flight scan and launch confirmation as `run_project`, and is refused while a runtime session is live on the same project. On Windows its window is not shown.
- `take_screenshot` returns pixel statistics on every call: `chromatic`, `dominant` and `distinct`, measured from the full-resolution PNG on a grid of about 8192 sample points (a 15 px step at 1920x1080), and a `likelyBlank` verdict decided over every pixel: `true` when the frame is one flat color within 8 of 255 per channel. A caller that cannot look at the image can tell a rendered frame from a blank one. A PNG wider or taller than 16384 pixels, larger than 8192 x 8192 pixels in total, or one that inflates past its declared size is not decoded: `stats` is `null` with a leading warning, and `render_movie` leaves that frame unmeasured.
- Several projects can run at once. `switch_project` points the runtime tools at another session, and `check_project` reports the current project and every live session.
- Profiler captures (`profile_project`, and `start_profiler` with `stop_profiler`) now also report `fps`, `slowFrames` counted against `targetFps`, and `monitors`: draw calls, memory, node, orphan and physics counts, pipeline compilations and custom monitors. Three opt-in additions go further. `visual: true` records the Visual Profiler, with CPU and GPU time per render stage keyed by group nesting, `(other)` rows for group time nothing covered, and the worst frame, and it switches itself off after three truncated frames in a row and says how to raise the limit. `timeline: true` (or `timelineMs`) records fps, frame budget, draw calls, render time and the top three items per interval, about 60 intervals at most. `track` samples up to four `NodePath:property` values from the running game and places them on the timeline; it is collected from the session that ran the capture and from no other. Nothing that was not measured reads as a number: a `visual` capture that folded no render frame leads with a warning instead of reading as free rendering, `fps`, `monitors` or a single monitor that could not be measured is `null` with a warning, a tracked path that never resolves is warned about, and `get_debug_output` explains the engine's timestamp overflow errors as profiler-caused.
- `run_project({ attach: true })` attaches to a Godot you launch yourself. It runs the pre-flight scan, spawns nothing, and `stop_project` ends it without killing your process.
- Structured responses on every tool. All 39 tools declare an `outputSchema`, return a matching `structuredContent`, and share field names across tools. Strict MCP clients that reject a missing `structuredContent` now work with every tool. Outcome fields come from what the engine did after the operation, not from the request, and the fields a tool returns on every success are marked `required` in its schema. `validate` is the exception: it declares none, because a single target and a `targets` batch return different fields.
- `set_node_properties` and `add_node` can set `metadata/<name>` on a node and any slash key the node declares with a type, such as `theme_override_colors/font_color`.
- Every tool description is at most 500 characters. Longer guidance moved into per-property descriptions and `docs/tools.md`.

## Fixed

- Calls such as `batch_scene_operations`, `set_node_properties` and `attach_script` no longer fail with `GDScript returned invalid JSON (Unexpected token 'G', "Godot Engi"...)` (#68). The result now travels on its own marked line of Godot's output, so the engine banner, a `[DEBUG]` line or anything a project autoload prints can no longer be mistaken for it. The marked line carries a token drawn fresh for each run, so a line a project script prints with the same marker, before the operation or after it, is not taken for the result.
- Edits on or under a node inside an instanced scene are no longer lost on save, and duplicating an instanced node no longer doubles its inner nodes or writes the copy as a plain node.
- A headless operation that fails now ends its Godot process with a non-zero exit code.
- The loss check behind the scene editing tools reads values that span several lines, matches `./Name` and `%UniqueName` node paths to the request (a `delete_nodes` written that way no longer warns about the nodes it deleted), follows a batch's save-as, and reports a lost placeholder, a lost `[editable]` line and lost stored values of an inline resource whose script failed. Overrides it cannot check against a non-text base scene are counted instead of guessed at.
- A scene that cannot be loaded or saved is an error instead of a success that says nothing was wrong.
- A failed final save in a batch, or a batch that named one scene two ways, no longer reports entries as saved when they were not or loses edits.
- A batch that changes a scene and a scene built from it (one that inherits or instances it) no longer saves the first scene's old values into the second as overrides. Such scenes are written dependents first, and a `save` item writes the dependents that hold unwritten operations ahead of the scene it saves.
- A batch item stopped by a script error, such as an `add_node` whose script has an `_init` with a required argument, is that item's error, and the rest of the batch still runs. It used to end the whole batch with no results.
- A `nodeType`, `rootNodeType` or `res://` property value written with a leading slash (`/../tool.gd`, `res:///../tool.gd`) or a drive prefix is refused as a path outside the project. On Godot 4.5 such a path loaded and ran a script from outside the project root.
- A property declared with a script `class_name` (`@export var stats: EnemyStats`) accepts a `.tres` of that class. It used to be refused as a plain `Resource`.
- `connect_signal` from or to a node inside an instanced scene saves the connection, and the scene gains an `[editable path=...]` line for that instance, as with any other edit inside one.
- A connection to the bridge port that sends no valid token no longer cancels a `simulate_input` batch that is running.
- `get_scene_tree` paths resolve when passed back to another tool, and a depth cut is marked instead of looking like a leaf.
- `validate` no longer reports a script with a parse error as valid when it was named `./a.gd`, with a backslash, or under a directory containing a space.
- `update_autoload` with `autoload_path` and `get_ui_elements` with `visible_only` now take effect. They used to be ignored while the call reported success. `add_autoload` and `remove_autoload` now accept `autoload_name` and `autoload_path`, which they used to reject with an error naming the camelCase parameter.
- `get_project_settings` reads `project.godot` values as Godot does: multi-line strings, escapes, comments, hyphenated section names, and a `[__proto__]` section that no longer alters later answers.
- The project file tools say what they could not read. An unreadable directory, a link they did not follow, a depth cut or a mistyped extension is reported instead of looking like a short answer.
- `stop_project` and `run_project` say when bridge cleanup could not be confirmed, and `run_project` reports an unreadable bridge owner registry at once.
- A server shutdown that landed while a game was still starting no longer leaves that game running with nothing tracking it, and a late bridge connection can no longer redirect or fail the next command after a `switch_project`.
- On Windows, headless Godot runs no longer paint their console text over the terminal that runs your MCP client, and `launch_editor` no longer lets the editor's output pipes fill up.
- The pre-flight script scan reads a member chain split by a line continuation or a comment, no longer loses an identifier after an unspaced `^`, and reports scripts it could not read instead of skipping them. A mis-set security flag such as `GODOT_MCP_STRICT=1` now prints a line to stderr at startup instead of being ignored without a word.
- The scene scanner behind the pre-flight scan reads `;` comments, indented headers and blanks around `=` in a header.
- A profiler capture that closed without the engine's totals packet is marked incomplete, and its `seconds` is no longer overstated.
- `profile_project` or `start_profiler` called after the game exited no longer discards the finished capture that `stop_profiler` can still read.
- A failed scene operation on a project whose autoloads print to stdout now leads its error with the operation's own reason (`Parent node not found: root/X`) instead of showing only the engine's exit-time lines. Errors from headless operations no longer point at `get_debug_output`, which reads a runtime session and never held their output.
- A scene result that itself contains the result marker text (a Label that quotes it, a node name echoed in a warning) is read whole instead of being reported as invalid JSON after the write had landed.
- `validate` with `checks` says why a scene could not be loaded for them, and no longer runs an asset import under a game another MCP server is running on the project.
- `run_project({ background: true })` never shows the game window on Windows, because the process is spawned hidden, and moves it off-screen after startup elsewhere, with mouse input passing through. The window no longer grows when it goes borderless, which had put injected click coordinates off target, and the description no longer promises that keyboard input is blocked.
- Path parameters accept `res://scenes/a.tscn`, `./scenes/a.tscn`, `scenes\a.tscn` and an absolute path inside the project everywhere. A `res://` `scenePath` used to fail the existence check in the standalone tools, an absolute `scene` argument was not scanned by the launch gate, and `add_autoload` now writes the `res://` form of an absolute in-project path.
- `run_project` and `render_movie` read `run/main_scene` with the `project.godot` grammar, and the repair of a stranded `McpBridge` entry finds a hand-written `McpBridge = "..."` line.
- A `tools/call` that names `constructor`, `toString` or `__proto__` answers MethodNotFound like any unknown tool, instead of calling a function inherited from `Object.prototype`.
- An attach no longer gives up early when Godot is launched seconds after `run_project` starts waiting: refused connections from before anything listens are not counted toward the give-up limit, which counts only once the port has accepted a connection. A bridge that reports its project path with a different letter case than the session was started with is no longer taken for another project's bridge.
- The advice after a failed attach says what is true: the failed attempt removed its bridge and every attach writes a new token, so a Godot that started during the failed wait cannot be attached to, and retrying with the same `bridgePort` does not change that.
- A start that is stopped, or fails, after it injected the bridge removes the bridge and its owner file, so no other server is told a session is running on the project until this one exits. A malformed bridge frame no longer leaves its socket listeners behind.
- A screenshot path is validated against the session the call was admitted for, so a `switch_project` that lands mid-call cannot make a path pass against another project.
- A capture left open when the game exits (`start_profiler`) is closed out as incomplete, so `stop_profiler` still ranks the frames it folded. A `profile_project` window cut off by an exit is an error that says to call `stop_profiler` when frames were kept. A capture started right after one that timed out is no longer ended early, and marked complete, by the earlier capture's late totals packet.
- The tip on a `run_script` result in an attached session says that `print()` output is not captured there, so `get_debug_output` has nothing to show.
- `bridgePort` is declared as an integer in the `run_project` schema, which is what the server already required.
- An attach whose bridge injection failed part-way no longer leaves the project marked as owned by this server until it exits, and a session that ends while its bridge cleanup is incomplete now says so on the error it returns.
